questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. If the sentence has no error, then select 'No error'.**

To whom did you give the packet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. No error

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• As we know that "who" is used for the **subject** of the verb, "whom" is used for the **object**
 
• In the case of** Passive voice- ** it swaps the **subject** and **object; **thus, the usage of the preposition '**to'** is correct because 'whom ' is the object of 'give to'
 
 
• **For e.g.-** Whom I talked **to**. [Here, '**I'** is the **subject** and '**whom'** is the **object** of** 'talked to'**]
 
 
 
• Also, **the subject of the sentence is 'you', the helping verb is 'did', the main verb is 'give', the object of the sentence is 'the packet' and the preposition 'to', the preposition always has a prepositional object, so 'whom' is the prepositional object which is written in the starting of the sentence.**
 
• Hence, the given sentence *is grammatically correct.*

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Much of the art he / discusses is funny, playing / and mischievous.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in the sentence is in the segment 'discusses is funny, playing'. The error lies in the usage of 'playing'. 
 
• The adjectives 'funny', 'playing' and 'mischievous' are used to describe the art.
 
• 'Playing' is a verb (participle) but in this context an adjective is required.
 
• Considering the context of the sentence (describing the nature of the art), it would be more appropriate to replace 'playing' with something like** 'playful' **to align with the adjectives **'funny'** and **'mischievous'.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **"discusses is funny, playing".**​

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is:* **"Much of the art he** discusses is funny, ******playful****** **and mischievous."*

and desiring to pursue her hobbies

questions.solution:

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

We noticed that most of the shoppers in the mall looking for packets of ready to cook food.

options.text: packets of ready to cook food

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'in the mall looking for'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

** In the given sentence,** the usage of **'in the mall looking for**' is incorrect Instead, use **'in the mall were looking for'**

 
• **According to grammar,** **'Most of'** is a quantifier which is used to **'to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.'**
 
• **In the given sentence,** **'that clause'** is used which has its own subject which is 'shoppers' hence we need a verb for this subject because it is not mentioned in the sentence. 
 
• *So we need a plural verb which should be in the past tense because the main clause of the sentence is in the past tense.*
 
• So use **'were looking'**

**So the correct sentence is- ***We noticed that most of the shoppers in the mall **were looking for** packets of ready to cook food.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

There is a whole world / out there that / is invisible from / the naked eye.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **is invisible from**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error here lies in the choice of the correct preposition.
 
• Replace "**from**" with "**to**" in order to correct the sentence.
 
• **From **is used to refer to the place where someone or something starts or originates.
 
• **To **is used to indicate the person or thing that receives or experiences the object of the verb.
 
• Here, the action is "**invisible**" and the receiver is "**the naked eye**."
 
• So, the preposition "**to**" should be used here.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 2**, which contains an error in it.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *There is a whole world out there that is invisible to __the naked eye.*

questions.question:

__

• In the given sentence, the **past perfect tense** should be used to show that the painting's value was underestimated before the present discussion.
 
• Correct use of the past perfect tense provides clarity in the sequence of events.

Hence, the correct statement is "***The art historian argued that the painting's value had been greatly underestimated__, and that its unique style and technique deserved recognition from the art community and the public alike*."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
